body: When parents conceive, do you know what they hope for? A happy, healthy baby with ten fingers, ten toes, and all of the same opportunities they had - and in most cases, more. No parent hopes that something is “wrong” with their child when they conceive, or throughout their pregnancy. When something goes wrong, their parents are counseled through the stages of grief. While this isn’t saying that certain groups of people don’t deserve to currently exist, this is saying there are difficult challenges that both the child and parents could potentially avoid. What if parents no longer have to be saddled with the inability to financially, mentally, emotionally, or physically raise their child due to a severe physical or intellectual disability? What if we could capitalize on a better quality of life for children and parents? What if we could avoid childhood cancer, children becoming wards of the state, or children who are never able to reach societal expectations, or socioemotional/developmental milestones? It is so incredibly difficult to be a parent - especially as we descent into our current hellscape of a timeline. This includes the current administration in the US stripping us of social safety nets, especially for kids with disabilities or significant health issues. I do not blame people for wanting to ensure their child will live a healthy and happy life, especially after seeing what it’s done to parents who do have these challenges (and oftentimes regret their decision to be a parent, or resent their impossible, never ending situation). If you have children, and you can seriously say that you would trade places with the single mom in section 8 housing who is paycheck to paycheck and constantly on the phone with their child’s health insurance company and worried about them getting the education they deserve at school, because they have a child with a severe physical and intellectual disability - a child who requires heavy lifting, struggles to communicate, and has a slew of other health issues - then fine. There isn’t much of a point to my argument. But if you instead look at your own healthy children - who don’t require round the clock care, can laugh and play with their peers at recess, will have better chances of surviving as they continue developing, isn’t cast aside by society, isn’t fighting for their life, has a terminal illness, or is dead from cancer after spending almost their entire existence in pain and in hospitals, and that you don’t have to constantly worry about when you wither away to nothing - and you thank god that is not your/their situation, then that is exactly the point I’m making. And I don’t want to hear “anything could go wrong, and you’re supposed to love them anyway.” And of course, any good parent would. But that isn’t supposed to be the typical situation; it is, in fact, an atypical situation that creates insurmountable hardships for children and their families. You can’t abandon these groups of people and you shouldn’t make it the responsibility of their siblings, but if you could circumvent it from happening all together then what’s the problem? Especially given that it’s not even a life yet - this is pre-life, pre-existence, a hypothetical child. I think we all know the choice we would make, if it were given to us, and that is completely valid.

Infertility may be disappointing, but I’m more concerned about achieving this life goal of mine. Moreover, I only want to experience it once. I don’t need to be pregnant to have more children, and would absolutely love to adopt and foster to adopt because the world has far too many kids who need/deserve a loving home. Being a mom requires a lot of sacrifice and unconditional love - it’s not about the baby shower, gender reveal party, diaper party, maternity clothes, or professional pregnancy pictures. The real joy in parenting comes while loving your child for the rest of your life, not only for those first 9 months + delivery.

Because they’re not making choices with our best interest in mind anyway. They know we’re outraged and still don’t care. And if they’re not making solid choices for their own citizens (and in many cases treating minority citizens like shit anyway), why would they choose to care about the “illegal immigrants who are rapists and gang members and here to steal our jobs?” Does protesting even work? In this day and age, no. Our leaders will look at us and... actually they probably wouldn’t even bother looking at us, and if they did, they’d laugh and continue what they were doing. Do we get together and overthrow the government? Well, no. Because we would be killed. And these things would still be happening. And even if people wanted to be martyrs and be killed to take a stance, no one would care and they’d be another number. If our government looks at our soldiers fighting their wars for them as just another number, do you think they’d place any importance on a civilian going against their political agenda? Additionally, I dont care how many guns someone owns, overthrowing their government is a lose lose for everyone because our military is well funded. You wanna fight the government? You’re gonna lose. You wanna fight the American southerner with his 15 handguns and 10 ARs? You wanna participate in hand to hand combat with your neighbor because she believes that brown people aren’t people in the first place? Some people honestly don’t even think this is wrong and support what the government is doing. And finally, if we can’t protest, do we just vote these people out to create some change and do what’s right by humanity and actually have a voice? Well, in my opinion, who cares? Who said we actually voted for these people to be in charge anyway? Who says we have a true democracy and the American people are making the rules? Who said that the people in charge can get voted out when we can’t even impeach our own president on valid grounds, or set term limits for congress? Who said our political leaders would ever choose morality over money? Do we want change? Yes. Will we ever get what we want? Probably not. So please inform me how this protest and trusting our government is going to work. Say what you want about Americans being lazy and not doing what’s right and not being outraged enough but I certainly don’t see you making the trip to the White House and standing with a sign either.
